body:
A human points at exact elements while talking to the design agent, and the agent knows what is meant by computation, without vision. Depends on the design agent (feature:aff58e018ae80474) and on the tabs that draw elements (feature:b993a7a21b436618, feature:7c9cdfad16609a44).

## Asked for

- A core requirement: a user can select a component or region and add a note to it. An agent can then work out exactly what is being called out by computation, without vision.
- The simplest form: a reference to an element ID and associated text.
- It is just something to point at elements with, for now.

## Decided

- **A note is one or more element IDs plus text**, sent with a chat message to the design agent.
- **A dragged-out region becomes the IDs of the elements inside it.**
- **A note is not kept on the design.** A note that stays is a narrative, which is not planned.
- Notes work alongside the chat. Chat is how the human talks to the agent; a note is how they point at something exact.

## From the other agent's plan (direction, not gospel)

- Clicking an element selects it by ID.
- It stored notes as IDs plus a path in the tree. Storing was dropped, but the path may still help an agent place an element.

## Suggested (cursory, not prescriptive)

- Selection reads the `data-design-id` the renderer puts on each element (feature:7c9cdfad16609a44), so pointing works the same on both tabs.

## Open

- What a region means when an element is only partly inside it.
- Whether a note can point at an edge on the Architecture tab as well as a node. The assumption is yes, since both are elements.

## Not in this feature

Notes that stay on a design, resolving notes, and notes from one agent to another.
title: design: notes
